note: Cross-check log. Every claim that may influence the rubric or advice is listed with its origin tier and a label: confirmed (found in a stored tier 1 extract, ids given), unconfirmed (not found in tier 1; usable as advice only, never moves a score), contradicted (tier 1 says otherwise; dropped and kept here as a log). Where tier 1 sources disagree, both are cited and 'governs' says which statement each one controls.

claims.text: Total statement limit is 4000 characters including spaces.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Each of the three answers needs at least 350 characters.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: At least 80% of the statement should emphasise interest in the programme (LSE).
claims.label: confirmed
claims.note: Full fetch: the archived LSE page also says at least 80%; the earlier 75% figure was a search error and is gone.

claims.text: Selectors look for evidence of critical engagement with the subject.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Selectors want the applicant's own views, not a description of what they read.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Joint degrees: give equal weight to each subject; a statement weighted to one side is significantly less competitive.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Academic interests should align with the programme applied for; missing subject commitment can end an application.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: One statement goes to every choice, so do not name a university or college.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Avoid discussing future career plans in Question 1.
claims.label: confirmed

disagreement.detail: UCAS Q1 guidance says that if you have a profession in mind you could talk about how the course will launch your career; Edinburgh asks you to show the implications for your career aspirations.
disagreement.governs: lse-ps governs Q1 of the main statement (LSE is the strictest lens). ed-what-you-need is satisfied by brief career material in Q2/Q3. For the Durham substitute statement no tier 1 source bans careers in Q1, so the check is advisory there.

claims.text: Each answer should add value; do not repeat information across questions.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Do not spend Q2 restating grades; universities see them elsewhere.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Q3 activities should be reflected on: why each is useful.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: AI-written statements risk rejection, withdrawn offers or a fraud finding; the applicant declares the statement is their own.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.note: The earlier disagreement with ucas-builder-old rested on a quote that the full fetch showed does not exist; removed.

claims.text: No software can currently detect AI, but every statement is read by admissions staff and AI writing "can be obvious" (Durham).
claims.label: confirmed

disagreement.detail: UCAS says its software checks for similarity and universities may be notified.
disagreement.governs: Both apply to every statement; neither changes scoring by itself, both support flagging AI-sounding phrasing.

claims.text: Selectors dislike list-like statements that describe what was studied rather than what was learned.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Reading counts only when the applicant says what they learnt, observed or found.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Correct use of subject terminology is a strength selectors look for.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Statements are similarity-checked; 10%+ similarity triggers human review and copied text can withdraw the application.
claims.label: confirmed

disagreement.detail: The older UCAS builder page says similarity greater than 30% is flagged.
disagreement.governs: ucas-similarity (applicant guide, 10%) is treated as governing; the builder figure is older.

claims.text: Writing only the 350-character minimum for Q3 is acceptable (LSE).
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Durham substitute statement: same 4000-character limit, plain text, read instead of the UCAS statement.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: For Social Sciences, Durham selectors look for originality and independence of thought and engagement with reading and research.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Durham Economics is taught with core micro, macro, data analysis and mathematical/statistical tools, ending in a dissertation.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: LSE Philosophy and Economics is taught with micro/macro, econometrics, logic or maths, PH103 and compulsory PH311 Philosophy of Economics.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Edinburgh scores statements for motivation, knowledge and exploration of the subject.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Edinburgh Philosophy and Economics year 1 covers logic, morality and value, history of philosophy, philosophy of science and Economics 1A/1B.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Edinburgh wants evidence the applicant understands the career implications of the choice.
claims.label: confirmed

disagreement.governs: Satisfiable in Q2/Q3 of the main statement; never in Q1.

claims.text: Q2 should focus on the most recent and relevant study and the skills it gave.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Q1 should show motivation and knowledge of the subject, backed by research.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: Reflection is rewarded over description in the 2026 format.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.note: Origin page (t3-uniguide-examples) is now missing behind a bot check, but the claim itself is confirmed by tier 1 (C-005, C-015). Scoring uses the tier 1 claims.

claims.text: Deeper reflection on fewer experiences adds more impact than many brief mentions.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: Origin page is unfetchable (bot check) and the claim has no tier 1 support, so it cannot be verified. Dropped and kept here as a log.

claims.text: Philosophy and economics statements need a specific concept or text to show real engagement.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: Origin page is unfetchable (bot check) and the claim has no tier 1 support, so it cannot be verified. Dropped and kept here as a log.

claims.text: The 80% must be spent in Questions 1 and 2; Q3 does not count toward it.
claims.label: contradicted
claims.note: lse-ps applies the 80% to the whole statement and says Q3 can 'expand on critical reflections' and hold super-curricular activity, so academic Q3 content counts. Dropped.

claims.text: Aim for around 500 words.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: The full fetch of the cited page does not contain "around 500 words"; the search summary misattributed it. Dropped and logged.

claims.text: Do not let AI write the statement.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: LSE expects applicants to fully use the space available on the UCAS form.
claims.label: confirmed

disagreement.detail: UCAS and Durham say nothing about filling the space; Durham warns against wasting characters.
disagreement.governs: lse-ps governs the main statement only; no space-use deduction for the Durham substitute.

claims.text: LSE expects spelling, punctuation and grammar to be checked and the statement to flow in a logical order.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: LSE's worked poor example: 'always dreamed ... since I was young' phrasing, naming LSE, listing IB subjects, and more space on an activity than on the subject.
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: There is no wrong question for a piece of information, and the 4000 characters may be split across answers in any way.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.note: Governs the reviewer: placement between Q2 and Q3 is never penalised; only missing content is.

claims.text: Avoid repetition, and avoid list-like writing even when it is written as a sentence (Durham).
claims.label: confirmed

claims.text: The three-question format is unchanged for 2027 entry.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: Tier 3, not officially confirmed. UCAS's guidance URL says '2026 entry onwards', but no tier 1 extract states it for 2027. Zero score impact.

claims.text: How much the statement counts varies by programme and is not published: for Edinburgh Law 2024/25, non-contextual applicants were differentiated by qualifications alone, and the scoring detail was withheld under FOI.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: Tier 2 (FOI decision), not officially confirmed for Philosophy and Economics. Does not contradict ed-competition ('for most programmes, we score personal statements'): Law may be an exception. Zero score impact.

claims.text: Published university guidance on personal statements often lacks transparency, and stated use can differ from actual practice.
claims.label: unconfirmed
claims.note: Tier 2 (named researchers; preprint). Not officially confirmed. It is the reason every score here is framed as a reading of published criteria. Zero score impact.

claims.text: Check spelling, grammar and punctuation before submitting.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.note: Confirmed by tier 1 (C-030). The engine does not spell-check; /review-ps flags errors it sees as issues citing C-030.
